"""Interactive conversational mode for the Agentic ODI CLI.

The chat is a small terminal REPL around an OpenAI-compatible model and the
Agentic ODI MCP server. It streams assistant text, executes MCP tool calls,
and keeps the conversation history in memory for the duration of the session.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import os
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Literal, Protocol

import typer
from core import ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT
from fastmcp import Client
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8001/v1"
DEFAULT_API_KEY = "local"
DEFAULT_MODEL = "local-tools-model"
DEFAULT_MCP_URL = "http://localhost:8000/mcp"

SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT
    + """

You are running in a terminal chat. Use the available MCP tools to create and
query Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes instead of inventing
records or IDs. Follow the ODI outcome statement format and flag opportunity
scores above 10 as underserved. Keep answers concise and readable as plain text.
"""
)

HELP_TEXT = """Commands:
  /help   Show this help
  /clear  Clear the conversation history
  /tools  List the MCP tools available to the assistant
  /exit   Quit (also /quit)

Anything else is sent to the ODI assistant."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChatConfig:
    """Connection settings for an interactive chat session."""

    base_url: str
    api_key: str
    model: str
    mcp_url: str

    @classmethod
    def from_env(
        cls,
        *,
        base_url: str | None = None,
        api_key: str | None = None,
        model: str | None = None,
        mcp_url: str | None = None,
    ) -> ChatConfig:
        """Resolve explicit values first, then environment variables, then defaults."""
        return cls(
            base_url=base_url or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL") or DEFAULT_BASE_URL,
            api_key=api_key or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY") or DEFAULT_API_KEY,
            model=model or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_MODEL,
            mcp_url=mcp_url or os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL") or DEFAULT_MCP_URL,
        )


class ChatSessionLike(Protocol):
    """The session surface the command handler needs."""

    tool_names: list[str]

    def clear(self) -> None: ...


def _to_openai_tools(tools: list[Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Translate FastMCP tool definitions into OpenAI function schemas."""
    return [
        {
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
                "name": tool.name,
                "description": tool.description or "",
                "parameters": tool.input_schema or {"type": "object", "properties": {}},
            },
        }
        for tool in tools
    ]


def _normalize_tool_calls(entries: dict[int, dict[str, str]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Turn the per-index streaming tool-call buffers into OpenAI tool calls."""
    return [
        {
            "id": entry["id"] or f"call_{index}",
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
                "name": entry["name"],
                "arguments": entry["arguments"] or "{}",
            },
        }
        for index, entry in entries.items()
    ]


def _tool_result_text(result: Any) -> str:
    """Extract readable text from an MCP tool result."""
    content = getattr(result, "content", None) or []
    parts = [getattr(item, "text", None) for item in content]
    text = "\n".join(part for part in parts if part)
    return text or str(result)


def handle_command(line: str, session: ChatSessionLike) -> Literal["exit", "handled"] | None:
    """Handle a slash command, or return None when the line is a chat message."""
    command = line.strip().lower()
    if command in {"/exit", "/quit"}:
        return "exit"
    if command == "/help":
        typer.echo(HELP_TEXT)
        return "handled"
    if command == "/clear":
        session.clear()
        typer.echo("Conversation cleared.")
        return "handled"
    if command == "/tools":
        if session.tool_names:
            typer.echo("\n".join(session.tool_names))
        else:
            typer.echo("No tools loaded.")
        return "handled"
    if command.startswith("/"):
        typer.echo(f"Unknown command: {line}. Type /help for commands.")
        return "handled"
    return None


class ChatSession:
    """A streamed tool-calling conversation against an OpenAI-compatible model."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        config: ChatConfig,
        openai_client: Any,
        mcp_client: Any,
        *,
        on_tool: Callable[[str, dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.config = config
        self.openai_client = openai_client
        self.mcp_client = mcp_client
        self.on_tool = on_tool
        self.messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]
        self.tools: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.tool_names: list[str] = []

    async def initialize(self) -> None:
        """Discover the MCP tools once and expose them to the model."""
        tools = await self.mcp_client.list_tools()
        self.tools = _to_openai_tools(tools)
        self.tool_names = [tool["function"]["name"] for tool in self.tools]

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Drop the conversation history but keep the system prompt and tools."""
        self.messages = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]

    async def _stream_completion(
        self, on_delta: Callable[[str], None] | None
    ) -> tuple[str, dict[int, dict[str, str]]]:
        stream: Any = await self.openai_client.chat.completions.create(
            model=self.config.model,
            messages=self.messages,
            tools=self.tools or None,
            tool_choice="auto" if self.tools else None,
            stream=True,
        )

        content_parts: list[str] = []
        tool_calls: dict[int, dict[str, str]] = {}

        async for chunk in stream:
            choices = getattr(chunk, "choices", None)
            if not choices:
                continue
            delta = choices[0].delta
            if delta is None:
                continue
            content = getattr(delta, "content", None)
            if content:
                content_parts.append(content)
                if on_delta is not None:
                    on_delta(content)
            for tool_call in getattr(delta, "tool_calls", None) or []:
                entry = tool_calls.setdefault(
                    tool_call.index, {"id": "", "name": "", "arguments": ""}
                )
                if tool_call.id:
                    entry["id"] = tool_call.id
                function = getattr(tool_call, "function", None)
                if function is not None:
                    if function.name:
                        entry["name"] = function.name
                    if function.arguments:
                        entry["arguments"] += function.arguments

        return "".join(content_parts), tool_calls

    async def _call_tool(self, call: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        name = call["function"]["name"]
        raw_arguments = call["function"].get("arguments") or "{}"
        try:
            arguments = json.loads(raw_arguments)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return f"Error: invalid JSON arguments for {name}: {raw_arguments}"
        if not isinstance(arguments, dict):
            return f"Error: arguments for {name} must be a JSON object"
        if self.on_tool is not None:
            self.on_tool(name, arguments)
        try:
            result = await self.mcp_client.call_tool(name, arguments)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            return f"Error calling {name}: {exc}"
        return _tool_result_text(result)

    async def ask(self, text: str, on_delta: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> str:
        """Send a message, execute any tool calls, and return the final text."""
        checkpoint = len(self.messages)
        self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": text})
        try:
            while True:
                content, tool_calls = await self._stream_completion(on_delta)
                if not tool_calls:
                    self.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": content})
                    return content

                normalized = _normalize_tool_calls(tool_calls)
                self.messages.append(
                    {"role": "assistant", "content": content or None, "tool_calls": normalized}
                )
                for call in normalized:
                    result = await self._call_tool(call)
                    self.messages.append(
                        {
                            "role": "tool",
                            "tool_call_id": call["id"],
                            "name": call["function"]["name"],
                            "content": result,
                        }
                    )
        except Exception:
            del self.messages[checkpoint:]
            raise


def _print_tool(name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    rendered = json.dumps(arguments, ensure_ascii=False)
    if len(rendered) > 100:
        rendered = rendered[:97] + "..."
    typer.secho(f"  → {name} {rendered}", fg="bright_black", err=True)


async def _run_chat(config: ChatConfig) -> int:
    typer.echo("Agentic ODI · interactive")
    typer.echo(f"model: {config.model}  ·  mcp: {config.mcp_url}")
    typer.echo("Type /help for commands, /exit to quit.\n")

    llm: Any | None = None
    try:
        async with Client(config.mcp_url) as mcp_client:
            llm = AsyncOpenAI(
                base_url=config.base_url,
                api_key=config.api_key,
                timeout=60.0,
            )
            session = ChatSession(config, llm, mcp_client, on_tool=_print_tool)
            await session.initialize()

            while True:
                try:
                    line = input("you › ").strip()
                except EOFError:
                    typer.echo()
                    break
                except KeyboardInterrupt:
                    typer.echo("\nUse /exit to quit.")
                    continue

                if not line:
                    continue

                action = handle_command(line, session)
                if action == "exit":
                    break
                if action == "handled":
                    continue

                typer.secho("odi › ", fg="green", bold=True, nl=False)
                printed = False

                def on_delta(piece: str) -> None:
                    nonlocal printed
                    printed = True
                    typer.echo(piece, nl=False)

                try:
                    await session.ask(line, on_delta=on_delta)
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                    typer.echo()
                    typer.echo(f"Error: {exc}", err=True)
                    continue
                typer.echo()
                if not printed:
                    typer.echo("(no response)")
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        typer.echo(f"Error: could not start chat: {exc}", err=True)
        typer.echo(
            f"MCP server: {config.mcp_url} (`python -m mcp_server`)\n"
            f"LLM endpoint: {config.base_url}",
            err=True,
        )
        return 1
    finally:
        if llm is not None:
            await llm.close()

    typer.echo("Goodbye.")
    return 0


def run_chat(config: ChatConfig) -> None:
    """Run the interactive chat until the user exits."""
    try:
        exit_code = asyncio.run(_run_chat(config))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        typer.echo("\nGoodbye.")
        return
    if exit_code:
        raise typer.Exit(code=exit_code)

def install_root() -> Path:

So the local backend exists but is only reachable programmatically via get_backend, and `outcomes` hardcodes `get_backend("mcp", ...)`. So `LocalBackend` is effectively dead code on main, and every `outcomes` command requires a running MCP server.

Wait, but main's README says CLI supports local backend? The README in this repo is from the branch. On main, README likely differs. Let me check main's README CLI section.

Key bugs on main:
1. **`LocalBackend.__init__` opens `SQLiteRepository(db_path=None)` immediately.** With db_path None, what does SQLiteRepository do? Need to check core on main. If it defaults to `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`, then even constructing LocalBackend (which happens in get_backend) touches the DB. But outcomes always forces MCP so LocalBackend isn't constructed by CLI. Hmm.

2. **`outcomes` commands are hardcoded to MCP** (`get_backend("mcp", mcp_url=mcp_url)`), so they fail if no server running, and there's no `--backend` global option. The local backend is unreachable from the CLI on main. That's a core-use-case break: the README/vision says you can use the CLI locally.

3. **Duplicate/incorrect `--version` handling**: `_version_callback(value: bool)` signature — Typer callbacks receive `(ctx, value)` or just value? In Typer, the callback is called with the parameter value only if it doesn't request ctx. Actually Typer inspects the callback signature; it can accept `value` or `ctx, value`. Here it's `value` only — fine. But then `version_cmd` is registered as a command named `version-cmd` (Typer converts function name `version_cmd` to command `version-cmd`), not `version`. So `agentic-odi version` triggers the callback? No — `version` isn't a command; `version-cmd` is. And `agentic-odi version` would be an unknown command. Wait, Typer uses the function name with underscores replaced by dashes → `version-cmd`. So the docstring says "Show CLI version" but the command is `version-cmd`. Potential bug: README/manual says `agentic-odi version`. Let me verify. On main, `version_cmd` → command name `version-cmd`. Hmm, that's a UX bug.

Actually wait — does Typer strip `_cmd`? No. So command is `version-cmd`. Let me verify by checking tests on main.

4. **`main` callback has no `invoke_without_command`** — default is False? Default for `invoke_without_command` is False, meaning the callback is NOT invoked when no subcommand. Actually Typer/Click: `invoke_without_command=False` means if no command is given, it prints help and exits. Hmm, default is False, so running `agentic-odi` with no args shows help. Fine.

5. **MCP client connection per call**: `_call_mcp` does `asyncio.run` per call, creating a new event loop and connection each command — acceptable for one-shot but slow. Also `MCP_URL_DEFAULT` is read at import time, so env var changes after import don't apply (minor).

6. **`MCPBackend.call` imports `cli.outcomes._call_mcp`** — circular-ish but lazy. Fine.

=== main: core/models.py ===
"""Core domain models for Agentic ODI."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from enum import Enum

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, computed_field


class Direction(str, Enum):
    MINIMIZE = "minimize"
    MAXIMIZE = "maximize"


class BusinessImpactCategory(str, Enum):
    REVENUE_GROWTH = "revenue_growth"
    COST_REDUCTION = "cost_reduction"
    RETENTION = "retention"
    RISK_MITIGATION = "risk_mitigation"
    OPERATIONAL_EFFICIENCY = "operational_efficiency"
    COMPLIANCE = "compliance"
    BRAND_REPUTATION = "brand_reputation"
    OTHER = "other"


def compute_opportunity_score(importance: float, satisfaction: float) -> float:
    """ODI Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)."""
    return float(importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0.0))


class Job(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the Job-to-be-Done")
    description: str | None = Field(None, description="Detailed description of the Job")


class Step(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this step belongs to")
    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the job step")
    order: int = Field(..., description="The chronological order of this step in the job map")


class Outcome(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
    step_id: str | None = Field(None, description="The ID of the specific Step, if applicable")
    statement: str = Field(
        ..., description="The desired outcome statement (e.g., 'Minimize the time it takes to...')"
    )
    importance: float | None = Field(None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Importance score (1-10)")
    satisfaction: float | None = Field(
        None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Current satisfaction score (1-10)"
    )
    opportunity_score: float | None = Field(
        None, description="Opportunity score (Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0))"
    )


class ValueMetric(BaseModel):
    name: str
    direction: Direction
    unit_of_measure: str
    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)

    @computed_field
    @property
    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)


class CustomerValue(BaseModel):
    direction: Direction
    unit_of_measure: str
    object_of_control: str
    contextual_clarifier: str | None = None
    statement: str
    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
    value_metrics: list[ValueMetric] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @computed_field
    @property
    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)


class BusinessValue(BaseModel):
    category: BusinessImpactCategory
    statement: str
    detail: str | None = None
    estimated_annual_value: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0)
    confidence: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0, le=1.0)


class CustomerOutcome(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
    step_id: str | None = Field(

=== main: core/models.py ===
"""Core domain models for Agentic ODI."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from enum import Enum

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, computed_field


class Direction(str, Enum):
    MINIMIZE = "minimize"
    MAXIMIZE = "maximize"


class BusinessImpactCategory(str, Enum):
    REVENUE_GROWTH = "revenue_growth"
    COST_REDUCTION = "cost_reduction"
    RETENTION = "retention"
    RISK_MITIGATION = "risk_mitigation"
    OPERATIONAL_EFFICIENCY = "operational_efficiency"
    COMPLIANCE = "compliance"
    BRAND_REPUTATION = "brand_reputation"
    OTHER = "other"


def compute_opportunity_score(importance: float, satisfaction: float) -> float:
    """ODI Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)."""
    return float(importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0.0))


class Job(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the Job-to-be-Done")
    description: str | None = Field(None, description="Detailed description of the Job")


class Step(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this step belongs to")
    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the job step")
    order: int = Field(..., description="The chronological order of this step in the job map")


class Outcome(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
    step_id: str | None = Field(None, description="The ID of the specific Step, if applicable")
    statement: str = Field(
        ..., description="The desired outcome statement (e.g., 'Minimize the time it takes to...')"
    )
    importance: float | None = Field(None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Importance score (1-10)")
    satisfaction: float | None = Field(
        None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Current satisfaction score (1-10)"
    )
    opportunity_score: float | None = Field(
        None, description="Opportunity score (Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0))"
    )


class ValueMetric(BaseModel):
    name: str
    direction: Direction
    unit_of_measure: str
    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)

    @computed_field
    @property
    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)


class CustomerValue(BaseModel):
    direction: Direction
    unit_of_measure: str
    object_of_control: str
    contextual_clarifier: str | None = None
    statement: str
    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
    value_metrics: list[ValueMetric] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @computed_field
    @property
    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)


class BusinessValue(BaseModel):
    category: BusinessImpactCategory
    statement: str
    detail: str | None = None
    estimated_annual_value: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0)
    confidence: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0, le=1.0)


class CustomerOutcome(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
    step_id: str | None = Field(
        default=None, description="The ID of the specific Step, if applicable"
    )
    customer_value: CustomerValue
    business_value: BusinessValue

    @computed_field
    @property
    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
        return self.customer_value.opportunity_score

Now I have a thorough understanding of main's CLI. Let me identify the core use cases and bugs concretely.

**Main CLI surface:**
- `agentic-odi --version` → prints `__version__` ("0.1.0")
- `agentic-odi version-cmd` → prints version (bug: docstring says "Show CLI version", but command is `version-cmd`, and README says `agentic-odi version`). Actually wait — let me verify Typer naming. Typer converts function name `version_cmd` to command name `version-cmd` by default. Yes. So `agentic-odi version` fails. This is a real bug.
- `agentic-odi outcomes add|get|list|update|delete|score ...` → **all hardcoded to MCP backend** via `get_backend("mcp", ...)`. Requires running MCP server.
- `agentic-odi connectors list|add|health|ingest`

**Core use cases** (per README/vision on main): manage Customer Outcomes (the ODI center of gravity on main), run connectors ingest, compute opportunity score, version/help.

**Now, the critical bugs / quality issues on main:**

1. **LocalBackend is unreachable and broken.** 
   - `outcomes` commands force `get_backend("mcp", ...)` — the local backend is never selected. So the CLI can't be used standalone; it requires a running MCP server.
   - `LocalBackend.update_customer_outcome` calls `service.update_customer_outcome(outcome_id, args)` where `args` includes `outcome_id` plus flat keys (`category`, `business_statement`, etc.) — the repository merges flat keys into the top-level model dict, which won't map `business_statement` → `business_value.statement`. So local updates are broken. Also `service.update_customer_outcome` → repo returns None on ValidationError, service raises NotFoundError, misleading.
   - `LocalBackend.__init__` eagerly constructs `SQLiteRepository(db_path=None)` → opens `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` and loads snapshot at construction. `get_backend("local")` thus touches disk even for `score`.
   
2. **`--version` / `version-cmd` duplication and naming bug.** `version_cmd` command name is `version-cmd`. README (branch) says `agentic-odi version`. Need to confirm main's README.

3. **Errors return exit 0.** `get_customer_outcome` returns `str(e)` (the raw exception message, e.g. the outcome_id string!). Wait: `CustomerOutcomeNotFoundError.__init__` calls `super().__init__(outcome_id)`, so `str(e)` is just the outcome_id — not even a human message. So `agentic-odi outcomes get missing-id` prints `missing-id` and exits 0. That's a glaring UX bug.

4. **`update`/`delete` not-found also print raw id or return None**; `update_customer_outcome` catches and returns `str(e)`.

5. **No `--backend`/`--db` global options on main.** The README on main may or may not document local. Need to check.

6. **Per-command `--mcp-url` duplication** on all outcomes commands; `MCP_URL_DEFAULT` computed at import time.

7. **`score` nested under `outcomes`** — awkward. README says? Check.

8. **Output is raw JSON** (no tables, no `--json`). For a "stellar" CLI, need readable default output + machine-readable option.

9. **Import-time cost**: `cli.py` imports `connectors` (which imports `connectors.factory`, registry, etc.) and `outcomes` (imports fastmcp at module top: `from fastmcp import Client`). So `agentic-odi --version` pays fastmcp + pydantic + connectors import cost. That's a startup performance issue. The parity branch fixed this with lazy import ("perf(cli): lazily import fastmcp client"), but that's not on main.

10. **`connectors ingest` only appends to in-process sink** — no persistence; `get_default_sink()` in-memory. Not necessarily a bug.

11. **`connectors.py` `_call_mcp` duplicate** — actually `outcomes._call_mcp` and `MCPBackend` importing it. Duplication.

12. **`version` string hardcoded "0.1.0"** vs pyproject 0.1.0 — off (release 0.2.0 on main per earlier log `8e09386 chore(main): release 0.2.0`? Wait that commit was on the feature branch listing main..HEAD, meaning it's not on main. Hmm. Let me re-check: the `git log main..HEAD` output included `8e09386 chore(main): release 0.2.0`. That means 8e09386 is in main..HEAD? No — `main..HEAD` lists commits reachable from HEAD but not main. 8e09386 appears, so it's NOT on main. But its message is "chore(main): release 0.2.0". Confusing but whatever. Actually wait, it could be that main is at a commit before 8e09386. Let me not worry.

Actually let me check main's tip and version. `git show main:cli/src/cli/version.py` → 0.1.0. And main's pyproject version 0.1.0. Fine.

13. **`typer.Typer(help=...)` but `main` callback `pass`** — `agentic-odi` with no args prints help. Fine.

14. **The `outcomes` group is registered with help "Manage Customer Outcomes" but the module docstring says "Customer Outcomes"; while `outcomes` in the vision should be *desired Outcomes*, and Customer Outcomes should be a separate group.** On main, `outcomes` = Customer Outcomes only. This naming mismatch is a design/quality issue. The branch renamed to `customer-outcomes`. For main's hardening, do we rename? That's a scope decision.

15. **No `jobs`/`steps`/desired-outcomes commands at all on main** — so core ODI use cases (define Job, capture desired outcomes) are impossible from the CLI. That's arguably the biggest functional gap. But the user said "harden the CLI currently on main" — scope is to make existing core use cases work well, not necessarily add the branch's new commands. However "core use cases work as designed" — what are the designed use cases on main? Customer outcomes + connectors + score.

Hmm. Need to check main's README to know what's documented/designed.

Let me read main's README CLI section and main's mcp_server tools. Also check main's connectors CLI test.

"""
run.py — Local dev launcher for Agentic ODI.

Starts the FastMCP server (``python -m mcp_server``) and the Streamlit client
(``client/app.py``) concurrently. Shutting down this script (Ctrl+C) terminates
both processes.

Usage:
    python -m client.run
"""

import os
import signal
import socket
import subprocess  # nosec B404 - launches only fixed child commands (see B603 notes)
import sys
import time

MCP_PORT = 8000
CLIENT_PORT = 8501
CLIENT_APP = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "app.py")


def is_port_in_use(port: int) -> bool:
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
        return s.connect_ex(("localhost", port)) == 0


def start_server() -> subprocess.Popen:
    if is_port_in_use(MCP_PORT):
        print(f"Error: Port {MCP_PORT} is already in use.")
        print("Please stop any process running on this port and try again.")
        sys.exit(1)

    print(f"Starting MCP server on http://localhost:{MCP_PORT}/mcp ...")
    # Fixed command, no shell, no untrusted input.
    return subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-m", "mcp_server"])  # nosec B603


def start_client() -> subprocess.Popen:
    if is_port_in_use(CLIENT_PORT):
        print(
            f"Warning: Port {CLIENT_PORT} is already in use. Streamlit might choose another port."
        )

    print(f"Starting Streamlit client on http://localhost:{CLIENT_PORT} ...")
    # Fixed command, no shell, no untrusted input.
    return subprocess.Popen(  # nosec B603
        [
            sys.executable,
            "-m",
            "streamlit",
            "run",
            CLIENT_APP,
            "--server.headless",
            "true",
            "--server.port",
            str(CLIENT_PORT),
        ]
    )

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from connectors.models import HealthStatus, IngestBatch, IngestRecord
from typer.testing import CliRunner

from cli.cli import app

ANSI_ESCAPE = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*m")
runner = CliRunner()


def _strip(text: str) -> str:
    return ANSI_ESCAPE.sub("", text)


def test_connectors_help_lists_commands() -> None:
    result = runner.invoke(app, ["connectors", "--help"])

    assert result.exit_code == 0
    output = _strip(result.output)
    assert "list" in output
    assert "add" in output
    assert "health" in output
    assert "ingest" in output


def test_connectors_list_empty(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    config = tmp_path / "connectors.json"
    result = runner.invoke(app, ["connectors", "list", "--config", str(config)])

    assert result.exit_code == 0
    assert "No connectors configured." in _strip(result.output)


def test_connectors_add_mcp_then_list(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    config = tmp_path / "connectors.json"
    add = runner.invoke(
        app,
        [
            "connectors",
            "add",
            "mcp",
            "--name",
            "gong",
            "--url",
            "http://localhost:9000/mcp",
            "--config",
            str(config),
        ],
    )
    listed = runner.invoke(app, ["connectors", "list", "--config", str(config)])

    assert add.exit_code == 0
    assert listed.exit_code == 0
    assert "gong" in _strip(listed.output)
    assert "mcp" in _strip(listed.output)
    payload = json.loads(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert payload["connectors"][0]["settings"]["url"] == "http://localhost:9000/mcp"


def test_connectors_add_rejects_duplicate(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    config = tmp_path / "connectors.json"
    args = [
        "connectors",
        "add",
        "mcp",
        "--name",
        "gong",
        "--url",
        "http://localhost:9000/mcp",
        "--config",
        str(config),
    ]
    runner.invoke(app, args)
    result = runner.invoke(app, args)

    assert result.exit_code == 1
    assert "already exists" in _strip(result.output)


def test_connectors_add_rejects_unknown_kind(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    config = tmp_path / "connectors.json"
    result = runner.invoke(
        app,
        ["connectors", "add", "rest", "--name", "jira", "--config", str(config)],
    )

    assert result.exit_code == 1
    assert "Unknown connector kind" in _strip(result.output)


def test_connectors_add_mcp_requires_url(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    config = tmp_path / "connectors.json"
    result = runner.invoke(
        app,
        ["connectors", "add", "mcp", "--name", "gong", "--config", str(config)],
    )

    assert result.exit_code == 1
    assert "--url is required" in _strip(result.output)


class _FakeConnector:
    def __init__(self, batch: IngestBatch | None = None) -> None:
        self.batch = batch or IngestBatch(connector_name="gong")

    async def health(self) -> HealthStatus:
        return HealthStatus(ok=True, message="reachable")

    async def ingest(self) -> IngestBatch:
        return self.batch


def test_connectors_health_uses_built_connector(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    config = tmp_path / "connectors.json"
    runner.invoke(
        app,
        [
            "connectors",
            "add",
            "mcp",
            "--name",
            "gong",
            "--url",
            "http://localhost:9000/mcp",
            "--config",
            str(config),
        ],
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr("cli.connectors.build_connector", lambda _config: _FakeConnector())

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["connectors", "health", "--name", "gong", "--config", str(config)])

    assert result.exit_code == 0
    assert "reachable" in _strip(result.output)


def test_connectors_ingest_appends_to_sink(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    config = tmp_path / "connectors.json"
    runner.invoke(
        app,
        [
            "connectors",
            "add",
            "mcp",
            "--name",
            "gong",
            "--url",
            "http://localhost:9000/mcp",
            "--config",
            str(config),
        ],
    )
    batch = IngestBatch(
        connector_name="gong",
        records=[
            IngestRecord(
                source_name="gong",
                source_kind="mcp",
                item_type="catalog",
                name="mcp-catalog",
                content="{}",
            )
        ],
    )
    sink = MagicMock()
    monkeypatch.setattr("cli.connectors.build_connector", lambda _config: _FakeConnector(batch))
    monkeypatch.setattr("cli.connectors.get_default_sink", lambda: sink)

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["connectors", "ingest", "--name", "gong", "--config", str(config)])

    assert result.exit_code == 0
    sink.append.assert_called_once()
    assert "gong" in _strip(result.output)

Now I have a very complete picture. Let me summarize the designed core use cases of main's CLI (per README):

1. `python -m cli --version` / `--help` / no args → help
2. `outcomes` (Customer Outcomes): add, get, list, update, delete, score — all as an MCP client (server must be running).
3. `connectors`: add/list/health/ingest.

Known bugs on main:
- **B1 `version_cmd` command name is `version-cmd`, not `version`.** README doesn't advertise `version` command though (only `--version`). Low impact but naming sloppiness. Actually README says "version and help information" and uses `--version`. So `version_cmd` is a duplicate with a dashed name. Minor.
- **B2 local backend unreachable + broken.** `outcomes` hardcodes MCP. No `--backend`. If MCP not running → all outcomes commands fail. That's "core use case" dependent on a server.
- **B3 error handling**: not-found → `str(e)` = raw id, printed to stdout, exit 0. Scripting can't detect. UX: `agentic-odi outcomes get bogus` prints `bogus`.
- **B4 `LocalBackend.update_customer_outcome` is wrong** (flat args merged at top level). Even if reached, nested business_value updates break. Also `Service.update_customer_outcome` returns None from repo → raises NotFoundError misleadingly on validation failure.
- **B5 import-time startup cost**: fastmcp imported at module import in `outcomes.py` (top-level `from fastmcp import Client`), and `cli.py` imports connectors + outcomes eagerly. `--version`/`--help` pay it. Performance.
- **B6 per-command `--mcp-url`, read at import time.** Duplicated 8x. Env changes ignored.
- **B7 `score` nested under `outcomes`**, though it's a top-level concept. Also `outcomes` means Customer Outcomes on main but the domain vocabulary "outcomes" = desired Outcomes. Naming confusion.
- **B8 no `--json`/human-readable output; raw JSON.**
- **B9 `LocalBackend` eagerly opens SQLite DB at construction** (SQLiteRepository.__init__). `get_backend("local")` touches disk; for `score` pure computation unnecessary.
- **B10 `MCPBackend.call` reaches into `cli.outcomes._call_mcp`** — layering inversion / duplicate of `_call_mcp`.
- **B11 duplicate `_call_mcp` logic in outcomes.py and backend.py** (branch fixed).
- **B12 `connectors` uses `Path.cwd()`** for default config path, so running from a different dir changes the registry location silently. README says `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` (relative). Could be intended.
- **B13 no `--backend`/`--db` global options**; local SQLite never exposed.
- **B14 `main` callback is `pass` and `invoke_without_command` default False → no command prints help. But `python -m cli` prints help. README says so. Fine.**
- **B15 `_version_callback(value: bool)`** — Typer callback param: if it declares only `value`, Typer supplies the value. OK.
- **B16 `MCPBackend` errors**: `_call_mcp` catches and prints to stderr, exits 1 — good. But there's a subtle issue: `_call_mcp` catches BaseException? No, `Exception`. If `asyncio.run` raises, fine.
- **B17 `connectors health` and `ingest` call `asyncio.run(connector.health())`** with no timeout handling; a hung connector blocks forever. `_call_mcp` has no timeout either (fastmcp Client default). Performance/robustness.
- **B18 `outcomes` commands don't validate job existence**, but MCP server does.
- **B19 no tests for local backend because it's unreachable** — test gap.
- **B20 `list_customer_outcomes` local uses json.dumps; MCP returns server text. Inconsistent output shapes.**
- **B21 `MCP_URL_DEFAULT` mutated at import → tests/CLI parity.**

Now, the user's definition: "stellar = user can go through the experience without bugs; core use cases work as designed; performant; quality experience Steve Jobs would support."

So the plan should focus on:
1. **Correctness** — fix bugs so core use cases work.
2. **Performance** — startup time, connection reuse, avoid disk/network on non-essential paths.
3. **Quality/UX** — readable output, honest exit codes/errors to stderr, consistent naming, helpful help text.

Now, a key scoping question: main's CLI only has Customer Outcomes + connectors. The "core use cases as designed" on main are those. But the ODI domain's core (Jobs, desired Outcomes) is only in MCP server, not CLI. The README roadmap on main says "CLI Dataset Commands: Extend cli/ so the ODI dataset can be created, queried, and scored from the terminal" is marked [x]... actually line 390 says `[x] **CLI Dataset Commands**`. Hmm but those commands don't exist on main. And the branch implemented them. This is confusing. The user explicitly said harden main's CLI, so I'll scope to what's on main and not import the branch's new command groups (that would be a feature, not hardening).

But wait — there's a real tension: should local backend be wired up on main? Main's LocalBackend supports only customer_outcome operations + compute_opportunity (no jobs/steps/desired outcomes). The MCP server has the full set. Main's README says "The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the server must be running." So the *designed* main experience IS MCP-client-only. Adding `--backend local` would be a feature (the branch did it). 

Given "harden... core use cases work as designed", I think the right scope is:
- Make the MCP-client experience rock-solid and performant.
- Fix the latent bugs in the dead-ish LocalBackend OR decide to remove it (dead code = quality issue). Hmm. Steve Jobs would remove unused code. But removing could break tests? There are no local tests on main. Actually LocalBackend is referenced only by `get_backend` and the branch tests don't exist on main. So on main it's genuinely dead code. Options: (a) wire it up properly (feature-ish), (b) remove it, or (c) fix and expose it.

I should ask the user which. This is a tradeoff worth their opinion. Actually the user said "harden based on CLI currently on main" and "core use cases work as designed". I'll ask a focused question about scope: do they want local (no-server) mode as a first-class supported path, or keep MCP-client-only and remove/fix dead code?

Also the naming/vocabulary: `outcomes` group = Customer Outcomes. Should we rename to `customer-outcomes` for clarity? That's a UX/quality call. The branch did rename. But that breaks the documented command. Worth asking.

Also: response format — add human-readable table vs keep JSON, add `--json`. 

Also: should we add the missing core commands (jobs/steps/desired outcomes) to main? That's the branch's work. Probably out of scope, but "core use cases" might include them. I'll ask.

Let me also verify the exact startup import cost to make performance claims concrete. I can't run main's code without a worktree. But I can reason: `python -m cli --version` → `cli/__main__.py` imports `cli.cli` → imports `cli.connectors` (connectors package: factory, models, registry, sink), `cli.outcomes` (fastmcp), `cli.version`. fastmcp imports are heavy. The branch commit "perf(cli): lazily import fastmcp client" confirms this was a real issue. So B5 is well-founded.

Let me also check connectors package on main to see if importing it pulls heavy deps (e.g., httpx/mcp). Let me check connectors/src on main.

Also check whether `connectors/__init__` imports heavy stuff.

Let me also look at the branch's fixes that are relevant to main — since the plan may port them. Specifically:
- `0ab167c fix(cli): accept an unset --backend in BackendConfig`
- `8e74a40 feat(cli): backend abstraction with full local tool dispatch and config resolution`
- `45453eb feat(cli): add interactive chat mode`
- branch's `cli.py` handles global --backend/--db/--mcp-url, startup auto-update, etc.

But the branch's CLI is quite different (it also has update paths, paths.py, _build_info). Porting wholesale would be a big feature merge, not a "harden main". So plan should be main-focused improvements, potentially borrowing specific fixes.

Let me quickly inspect connectors on main for import weight and any bugs.

Let me also check main's CI workflow to know what checks must pass.

Let me gather the last bits, then ask scoping questions.

"""Kind registry that maps connector configs onto Connector implementations."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable

from connectors.mcp.connector import MCPClientConnector
from connectors.models import ConnectorConfig, McpConnectorSettings
from connectors.protocol import Connector
from connectors.registry import UnknownConnectorKindError

Builder = Callable[[ConnectorConfig], Connector]

_builders: dict[str, Builder] = {}


def register_kind(kind: str, builder: Builder) -> None:
    """Register a builder for a connector kind (mcp today; others later)."""
    _builders[kind] = builder


def known_kinds() -> set[str]:
    return set(_builders)


def build_connector(config: ConnectorConfig) -> Connector:
    try:
        builder = _builders[config.kind]
    except KeyError:
        raise UnknownConnectorKindError(config.kind) from None
    return builder(config)


def _build_mcp(config: ConnectorConfig) -> Connector:
    settings = McpConnectorSettings.model_validate(config.settings)
    return MCPClientConnector(name=config.name, settings=settings)


register_kind("mcp", _build_mcp)

<skill_content name="writing-plans">
# Skill: writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Step Granularity

**Each step is one action with a checkable result:**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

## Review Focus

[The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
— one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
owns the code, in that task's own step style.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `function(input: InputType) -> ResultType` in `exact/path/to/file.py`**

One line on the approach when the signature and the test leave a choice
(which library call, which data structure); a code block only for an
algorithm they do not determine.

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## What a Step Contains

A step is done when the implementer can write exactly one reasonable thing
from it. That is the whole requirement: unambiguous, not complete. Each kind
of step carries what makes it unambiguous and nothing more:

- **A test step:** the test's name and its assertions, as code, with the
  spec's exact values in them.
- **A code step:** the exact signature (name, parameters, return type), the
  file it lives in, and the specific values the spec pins. The implementer
  writes the body. A body appears only for an algorithm the signature and
  tests do not determine, or for exact copy the spec fixes.
- **A verification step:** the command to run and the output that means it
  passed.
- **A reference to another task:** that task's Interfaces block says what
  to use; the plan does not repeat that task's code.

A plan is the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone. A plan
longer than the code it describes has written the code instead. Lines that
decide nothing ("TBD", "handle edge cases", "add appropriate validation",
"write tests for the above", a type or function no task defines) are the
opposite failure, and the self-review catches both.

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Step scan:** Every step must let the implementer write exactly one reasonable thing, and no step may carry more than that: a line that decides nothing is a gap, a function body the signature and tests already determine is a transcript. Fix both.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

**4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.

**5. Proportion:** Compare the plan's length to the spec's. A plan several times longer than the spec it implements is a transcript of the program, not a plan. If code blocks are most of the document, replace bodies with signatures, test names and assertions, and check that each step is still unambiguous.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving and self-reviewing the plan, link it for your human partner
to read. If they have already explicitly supplied an execution method, ask
them to review the plan and confirm it captures what they want; wait for that
review before implementation, then use the preserved method. Otherwise, ask
them to review the plan and choose an execution method before implementation.

**When no execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Which execution approach would you prefer?**

- **Subagent-driven** - A fresh subagent implements each task and a fresh reviewer checks it before the next one starts, then a whole-branch review at the end. Most thorough; costs a fresh context per task and per review.
- **Native** - I implement every task myself in this session, the way this harness runs work, then one fresh reviewer on the most capable model checks the whole branch. Cheapest and fastest; no independent review until the end. Runs well with a mid-tier session model, since the plan carries the design.

**For this plan I recommend <one of the two>, because <one sentence from the plan: how much the tasks depend on each other's interfaces, how many there are, what a shipped mistake would cost>. Does the plan capture what you want, and which approach should we use?"**

**When an execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Does it capture what you want?"**

**If Subagent-driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development

**If Native chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans

"""Append-only Intent Store (CTO specification)."""

import json
import sqlite3
from datetime import datetime


class IntentStore:
    def __init__(self, db_path: str = "intent_store.db") -> None:
        # Connect to SQLite in WAL mode for high-performance concurrency
        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
        self.conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;")
        self._init_db()

    def _init_db(self) -> None:
        """Creates an immutable, append-only event table."""
        with self.conn:
            self.conn.execute(
                """
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                    timestamp TEXT NOT NULL,
                    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
                    payload TEXT NOT NULL
                )
            """
            )

    def append(self, event_type: str, payload: dict) -> None:
        """Appends a new event to the stream (Immutable write)."""
        timestamp = datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
        payload_json = json.dumps(payload)
        with self.conn:
            self.conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO events (timestamp, event_type, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                (timestamp, event_type, payload_json),
            )

    def get_stream(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Retrieves the full chronological event stream for AI reasoning."""
        cursor = self.conn.cursor()
        cursor.execute("SELECT id, timestamp, event_type, payload FROM events ORDER BY id ASC")
        return [
            {
                "id": row[0],
                "timestamp": row[1],
                "type": row[2],
                "payload": json.loads(row[3]) if row[3] else {},
            }
            for row in cursor.fetchall()
        ]

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear all events (for testing)."""
        with self.conn:
            self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM events")

    def close(self) -> None:
        self.conn.close()
